solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Record struggle for club player?

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to jockey is to struggle or jostle for position

explanation.surface: A golfer or footballer fights over a recording, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club player' suggests a golfer or footballer; here the club is a nightclub and the player plays records.
explanation.definitionFit: A DJ plays records to dancers at a nightclub, a playful description signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: One using colours of very poor quality, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear the word spoken rather than see it written

parts.note: dire means dreadful, of very poor quality

explanation.surface: Someone whose painting or dyeing work is shoddy, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer is a tradesperson who colours fabric, so applies colours as a job.

clue.text: Son needs head covering in strong draught

parts.note: a wig covers the head

explanation.surface: A boy needs a hat to keep out a powerful cold wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draught' looks like a cold current of air; it is a long gulp of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large mouthful of drink, and a draught is also a gulp of liquid.

clue.text: Light lifting device round channel navy used to hold tons

parts.note: a jack lifts a car
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the pair of channel and navy are made to contain the tons

parts.note: a lane is a channel, as in a shipping lane
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Instructions for a crane rigged around a waterway, with the navy hauling heavy loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-o'-lantern is a hollowed pumpkin lamp, so it gives light.

clue.text: Vehicle made to carry a weight

indicators.note: the vehicle is forced to have the a placed inside it

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: A truck forced to haul a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a unit of mass for gemstones, equal to 200 milligrams.

clue.text: Fan, perhaps, of decommissioned vehicle?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in service
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An enthusiast of a vehicle that has been taken out of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' reads as an enthusiast; it is the electric kind that draws air out.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan pulls stale air out of a kitchen or bathroom; a fan is one example of an extractor.

clue.text: Change hands over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for hands is read backwards

parts.note: paws is informal for hands

explanation.surface: Pass something from one hand to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, an everyday synonym for change.

clue.text: Foot could be protected by this prime minister

definitions.text: Foot could be protected by this

definitions.meaning: the Duke of ... was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: Michael Foot, the Labour leader, sheltering behind a premier.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot was a British Labour leader, which makes 'Foot' look like a person; here it is the body part a boot protects.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington is a waterproof boot named after the Duke, who served as prime minister in 1828–30.

clue.text: Commit to preserve right for upper class

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter stands where the other was

parts.note: to perpetuate is to make something last, to preserve it
U denotes upper class in British usage

explanation.surface: Pledging to keep a privilege for the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right for upper class' means R takes the place of U. 'Commit' looks like pledge; it means carry out a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a crime is to carry it out, the same sense as committing one.

clue.text: Draw a secretive cuckoo

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are put into a mad new order

explanation.surface: Sketching a cuckoo that keeps itself hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like sketch; it is the cook's sense of gutting a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a fowl is to remove its entrails, which is what eviscerate means.

clue.text: Obscure promotion, dismissing second book

indicators.note: the second occurrence of the book letter is sent away from the promotion

parts.note: a blurb is promotional text on a book cover

explanation.surface: Little-known publicity that turns down a sequel.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur is to make something indistinct, which is to obscure it.

clue.text: Article in wood is parking light seen at night

indicators.note: in places the article inside the wood

parts.note: willow is a wood, used for cricket bats
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece claims a forest car park is lit after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A will-o'-the-wisp is a flickering phosphorescent glow over marshes, glimpsed after dark.

clue.text: Criterion was reformulated in a different way

indicators.note: reformulated means reworked, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A standard was rewritten so it now reads differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrariwise means conversely or the other way round, so done otherwise.

clue.text: Scrooge, perhaps keeping large amount in rough casket

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece sits inside the other
rough means roughed up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a heap is a large amount

explanation.surface: Dickens's miser hoarding a fortune in a crude box.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge in Dickens's A Christmas Carol is the classic miser, an example of a stingy person.

clue.text: Rich oppress our organising

indicators.note: organising means arranging, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: The wealthy are arranging to keep us down.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means flourishing financially, a direct synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: Plant collector finding her way around island

indicators.note: around means the other pieces go either side of the island

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: A botanist travelling about an island in search of flora.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist gathers and uses medicinal herbs, so collects plants.

clue.text: Like children lined up around worker?

indicators.note: around means the lined up phrase goes either side of the worker

parts.note: in file means lined up one behind another
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Pupils queueing around a teacher or worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantile means typical of infants, so childish.

clue.text: Gun control is reversed, not gradually eroded

indicators.note: is reversed tells us to read what remains backwards
not tells us to leave the eroded letters out

parts.note: to regulate is to control
ate, as in ate away, means gradually eroded

explanation.surface: Gun regulation goes into reverse instead of fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ATE leaves REGUL, which 'is reversed' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol, so a type of gun.

clue.text: Bachelor leaves dog something valuable

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so this letter comes out of the dog

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged hound

explanation.surface: A single man walks out and leaves his dog, his prized possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable thing or quality.

clue.text: Start January by visiting and opening base

parts.note: first means the opening one
the foot is the base of something

explanation.surface: Begin the new year by calling round and opening a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: First-footing is a Scottish Hogmanay custom: being the first person to cross someone's threshold after midnight on New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: To first-foot is to be the first visitor of the New Year, so it opens January with a visit.

clue.text: Second trial dropped in place of overall cuts?

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in court
shed means dropped, as leaves are shed

explanation.surface: A retrial dropped because of broad budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overall cuts' sounds like spending cuts; it is cutting the whole fleece off sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearing shed is where sheep have their entire fleece clipped off, the whole-body cut the cryptic hint suggests.

clue.text: Butterfly perched on the first down, regularly

parts.note: sat means perched

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of that answer

parts.note: the answer to 1 down, the first down clue

explanation.surface: A butterfly settled on the first feathers, at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first down' is the answer to 1 Down, DYER; taking its even letters gives YR.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs are a family of brown butterflies, such as the meadow brown.

clue.text: Earthmovers removing sleepers and rubbish

indicators.note: removing means taking the sleepers out of the earthmovers

parts.note: bulldozers move earth
dozers are people who doze, sleepers

explanation.surface: Diggers clearing away railway sleepers and debris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleepers' looks like railway timbers; it means people dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for nonsense, short for bullshit.

clue.text: Girl arrested at Stonehenge starts to excavate some stones

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of each following word

explanation.surface: A woman detained at the ancient monument after beginning to dig up some stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess Durbeyfield, heroine of Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles, is arrested at Stonehenge near the novel's end.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's heroine is captured by police while sleeping on the altar stone at Stonehenge.

clue.text: Prophet of a second coming before end of Christmas

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A prophet foretelling a Second Coming at the close of Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor Old Testament prophets, with a book of the Bible named after him.

clue.text: Circulate, but it's dire going around

indicators.note: going around means the letters are circulated into a new order

explanation.surface: Pass it round, though what is being passed is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to hand out or spread around, the same as circulate.

clue.text: A piece of cake is lardy, lacking in grain

indicators.note: lacking in means without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: lardy means fatty, greasy
GR is the abbreviation for grain, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A slice of cake is fatty and short of wholegrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' looks like literal cake; it is the idiom for something simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for a task that is simple and effortless.

clue.text: Mice emptied place for grain left over in London, say

indicators.note: emptied means the inner letters are removed, leaving just the outside ones
over means the storage place and the side are read backwards together

parts.note: a silo stores grain
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Mice cleaned out a grain store left behind in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mice emptied' keeps ME; 'over' turns SILOPORT into TROPOLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: London is an example of a great capital city, a metropolis.
